events.text: Handoff diagnosis (join not detected) is FALSIFIED: unit test with the exact reported coords passes — bp_2883 trims to 128.75 and emits 1 miter. Real bug is corner-miter PRISM placement: addCornerMiter uses hardcoded joinV*0.125 / nominalEnd-0.125 offsets instead of the wall's actual depth band, so miters land off the true corner square → slivers stick out. Investigating.

resolution: Fixed broken wall L-corner connection pieces (gaps + triangular slivers in the screenshots). The handoff's diagnosis (join not detected) was falsified — the join IS detected and the wall trims; the real bug was the corner-miter PLACEMENT. addCornerMiter hardcoded the corner square at a half-thickness offset that only lands right when both walls are floor-offset toward the corner. Real rooms use PAINTED-tile floors (no support plate), so walls stay centered and the miter was shoved half a thickness off its crossing — see-through gap on two sides, sliver overhang on the other two. Fix places the miter on the true crossing square = (this wall's depth band) × (partner's depth band): wallJoinRunLimits now carries squareU per joined end (partner band read as it renders, lifted onto its floor) and the mitered core-trim follows squareU so the core abuts the miter with no gap. Collision/run-extension unchanged. wallSlabs/placed/build suites green, full game compile+bake+render green.
